tiles.label: Dear Someone
tiles.defaultTopic: a letter to someone who will never read it in time
tiles.promptSeed: Write a letter from one person to another, set in a specific past era, addressing something left unsaid, written with the specific texture and constraints of its time.
tiles.description: A letter written to someone who will never read it in time.

tiles.label: The Unsent Letter
tiles.defaultTopic: a letter written but never mailed, found long after
tiles.promptSeed: Write a letter that was written but never sent, discovered decades later, addressing something the writer couldn't bring themselves to say out loud at the time.
tiles.description: A letter written but never mailed, found long after.

tiles.label: Found in the Attic
tiles.defaultTopic: a stack of old letters, and the life they quietly reveal
tiles.promptSeed: Describe discovering a bundle of old letters in an attic or estate, and what the fragments reveal about a life lived long before, focusing on small telling details.
tiles.description: A stack of old letters, and the life they quietly reveal.

tiles.label: Words Across Time
tiles.defaultTopic: two letters, written decades apart, that echo each other
tiles.promptSeed: Present two brief letter excerpts written decades apart by different people, whose sentiments unexpectedly echo one another, without direct commentary connecting them.
tiles.description: Two letters, written decades apart, that echo each other.

tiles.label: The Old Diner
tiles.defaultTopic: a diner that hasn't changed, in a town that has
tiles.promptSeed: Describe returning to a small-town diner unchanged since childhood, noting the contrast between its stillness and everything else that's moved on.
tiles.description: A diner that hasn't changed, in a town that has.

tiles.label: Main Street
tiles.defaultTopic: walking the same street, decades apart
tiles.promptSeed: Describe walking down a small town's main street, overlaying memory of what used to occupy each storefront onto what's there now.
tiles.description: Walking the same street, decades apart, remembering what stood where.

tiles.label: Summer, Long Ago
tiles.defaultTopic: a single specific summer, remembered in fragments
tiles.promptSeed: Write about a specific remembered summer from years past, using concrete sensory fragments rather than a full narrative — the sound, the light, one particular afternoon.
tiles.description: A single specific summer, remembered in fragments.
constraints: Fragmentary, not a full linear story

tiles.label: The House on the Corner
tiles.defaultTopic: a house that held a whole neighborhood's stories
tiles.promptSeed: Describe a specific house in a small town remembered for the role it played in the neighborhood's life, and what it's become since.
tiles.description: A house that held a whole neighborhood's stories.

tiles.label: Before the War
tiles.defaultTopic: an ordinary day, in the last stretch of before-times
tiles.promptSeed: Write about an ordinary day in a specific historical period shortly before a major upheaval, with the reader's hindsight creating dramatic irony the characters don't have.
tiles.description: An ordinary day, in the last stretch of before-times.

tiles.label: A Different World
tiles.defaultTopic: a single day, lived by the rules of another era
tiles.promptSeed: Write about a single ordinary day as lived under the specific social norms and constraints of a distinct past era, grounded in concrete daily detail rather than commentary.
tiles.description: A single day, lived by the specific rules of another era.

tiles.label: The Way Things Were
tiles.defaultTopic: an elder's memory of how things used to be done
tiles.promptSeed: Write in the voice of someone older recalling how a specific everyday task or custom used to be done, addressed to someone younger who's never known it any other way.
tiles.description: An elder's memory of how things used to be done.

tiles.label: Turn of the Century
tiles.defaultTopic: standing at the edge of one century, looking into the next
tiles.promptSeed: Write about someone at a literal turn of the century, reflecting on the change in the air and what they hope or fear the new era will bring.
tiles.description: Standing at the edge of one century, looking into the next.

promptSeed:
[SYSTEM]
You are NarraWeave, a creative writing engine focused on evocative historical and nostalgic writing in English. Your output is period-appropriate, sensory, and never anachronistic in tone.

[MODE]
Produce only the creative output. No titles, no preambles, no explanations, no meta-commentary. The piece should stand entirely on its own.

[TILE]
{{tile.promptSeed}}

[CONSTRAINTS]
- Output ONLY the creative piece — nothing else.
- Follow the structural rules of the selected form exactly (paragraph and word limits).
- Maintain period-appropriate voice and detail.
- Avoid modern phrasing or anachronistic references.
